judged_text: The public members endpoint takes limit and offset straight from user params with no clamping, removing the previous hard cap of 200 rows for automatic groups and allowing arbitrarily large LIMIT values. A client passes limit=9999999 on any group that passes guardian.ensure_can_see! and forces the server to load and serialize the entire membership in one request — a memory/CPU amplification vector on large groups, and full member-list enumeration beyond the 200-row ceiling the old code imposed on automatic groups.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff now does `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and applies it directly to `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound/clamping. Previously, for automatic groups it enforced `limit = (params[:limit] || 200).to_i` (effectively providing a hard ceiling of 200 by default, and only allowing pagination in that case). With the new code, any caller who can hit `/groups/:id/members` can pass an arbitrarily large `limit`, causing the server to load and serialize a very large member set in one request (CPU/memory amplification).
